title: Dimensional Shader Rift Editor
description: A virtual city sits beside a dungeon scene with a floating corset artifact between them acting as a dimensional rift anchor. The user manipulates custom post-processing shaders across both environments — adjusting chromatic aberration, dissolve boundaries, energy flow direction, and color grading — while a conservation law ensures total shader energy distributed across the three objects always sums to a fixed budget. Full undo/redo tracks every parameter change.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load VirtualCity.glb on the left, dungeon_warkarma.glb on the right, and Corset.glb floating centered between them, slightly elevated. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,10) looking at origin. Add ambient light (0.3) and two directional lights with slight color tints (warm left, cool right). Write three custom ShaderMaterial uniforms applied as post-process-style screen quad OR directly replace materials on each loaded model: (1) uDissolve (0-1 float controlling a noise-based dissolve edge glow), (2) uChromatic (0-1 controlling RGB channel offset intensity), (3) uEnergyColor (vec3 tint). Implement a CONSERVATION LAW: a total energy budget of 3.0 is shared among the three objects. Each object has an energy slider (0.0-3.0). When one slider increases, the others proportionally decrease to maintain the sum at exactly 3.0. Energy drives dissolve intensity and chromatic aberration strength per object. Add an HTML panel with: 3 energy sliders (coupled via conservation), a dropdown to select active object, a color picker for the selected object's uEnergyColor, a 'Flow Direction' toggle that animates dissolve noise scrolling left-to-right or right-to-left via a uniform uTime multiplier sign, and a 'Glow Intensity' slider controlling emissive edge brightness on dissolve boundaries. Implement full undo/redo with Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y storing snapshots of all slider values, colors, and toggle states in a history stack (max 50 entries). Each slider change, color pick, or toggle commits a snapshot. Display current step as 'History: X/Y' in the UI. The dissolve shader should use a simplex or value noise function in GLSL, with edges emitting bright color based on uEnergyColor multiplied by glow intensity. Ensure smooth 60fps animation with requestAnimationFrame updating uTime. Total interaction steps: adjust 3 energy sliders, pick 3 colors, toggle flow direction, adjust glow, plus undo/redo operations — yielding 10-14 meaningful steps.
